question.text: Given the triangle above, find the length of $\overline{BC}$ rounded to one decimal place.
question.explanation:
For an angle $\theta$ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

  • $\sin\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}$

  • $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{adjacent leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}$

  • $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{adjacent leg}}$

First, note that we are given the length of the hypotenuse $\overline{AB}$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overline{BC}$ adjacent to the given angle $\angle{B}.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the adjacent leg to the hypotenuse is cosine. Hence, \begin{align} \cos(m\angle{B}) &= \dfrac{\textrm{adjacent leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}} \\[5pt] \cos(38^\circ) &= \dfrac{BC}{12} \\[5pt] BC &= 12\cos(38^\circ). \end{align}

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that \begin{align} BC &= 12\cos(38^\circ) \\[5pt] &= 12(0.788\,01 \ldots) \\[5pt] & = 9.456\,12\ldots \\[5pt] &\approx 9.5, \end{align} rounded to one decimal place.

question.text: Given the triangle above, find the length of $\overline{AC}$ rounded to one decimal place.
question.explanation:
For an angle $\theta$ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

  • $\sin\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}$

  • $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{adjacent leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}$

  • $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{adjacent leg}}$

First, note that we are given the length of the adjacent leg $\overline{AB}$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overline{AC}$ hypotenuse to the given angle $\angle{A}.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the adjacent leg to the hypotenuse is cosine. Hence,

\begin{align} \cos(m\angle{C}) &= \dfrac{\textrm{adjacent leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}} \\[5pt] \cos(22^\circ) &= \dfrac{7}{AC} \\[5pt] AC\cdot \cos(22^\circ)&=7 \\[5pt] AC &= \dfrac{7}{\cos(22^\circ)}. \\[5pt] \end{align}

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that \begin{align} AC &= \dfrac{7}{\cos(22^\circ)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7}{(0.927\,18\ldots)} \\[5pt] &= 7.549\,74\ldots \\[5pt] &\approx 7.5, \end{align} rounded to one decimal place.

question.text: A triangle $\triangle LMN$ has $m\angle L = 90^\circ,$ $ m\angle N = 37^\circ,$ and $ LM = 8.$ Find the length of $\overline{LN}$ rounded to the nearest integer.
question.explanation:
For an angle $\theta$ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

  • $\sin\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}$

  • $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{adjacent leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}$

  • $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{adjacent leg}}$

First, let's sketch the given triangle.

Notice that we are given the length of the leg $\overline{LM}$ opposite to the given angle $\angle N$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overline{LN}$ adjacent$\angle N.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite leg to the adjacent leg is tangent. Hence, \begin{align} \tan(m\angle{N}) &= \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{adjacent leg}} \\[5pt] \tan(37^\circ) &= \dfrac{8}{LN} \\[5pt] LN\cdot \tan(37^\circ)&=8 \\[5pt] LN &= \dfrac{8}{\tan(37^\circ)}. \end{align}

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that \begin{align} LN &= \dfrac{8}{\tan(37^\circ)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8}{(0.753\,55 \ldots )} \\[5pt] &= 10.616\,35 \ldots \\[5pt] &\approx 11, \end{align} rounded to the nearest integer.
